hooks.text: One star could soon shine as bright as the Moon.
Will this giant star actually destroy our solar system?
This star isn't exploding, it just burped a cloud.

title: When Betelgeuse Explodes
description: Betelgeuse is a red supergiant so large it would swallow the inner solar system. Its eventual supernova will be bright enough to see during the day.

beats.text: One star could soon shine as bright as the Moon.
beats.visual: artist impression of a supernova in a dark night sky

beats.text: It's Betelgeuse, the red supergiant in Orion's shoulder.
beats.visual: widefield telescope image of the constellation Orion featuring Betelgeuse

beats.text: If it replaced our Sun, it'd swallow Earth and Mars.
beats.visual: diagram comparing the size of Betelgeuse to the Solar System planetary orbits
queries: Betelgeuse size comparison solar system diagram

beats.text: It is a runaway giant speeding through the galaxy.
beats.visual: Akari space telescope far-infrared composite image of Betelgeuse's bow shock
queries: Akari Betelgeuse bow shock FIS infrared

beats.text: It dimmed enough in 2019 to trigger explosion fears.
beats.visual: ESO VLT SPHERE images comparing Betelgeuse before and during the Great Dimming

beats.text: Hubble found it just burped a massive, cooling dust cloud.
beats.visual: artist's illustration of Betelgeuse ejecting plasma that cools into dust
queries: Betelgeuse surface mass ejection artist impression

beats.text: We're safe since it's five hundred light-years away.
beats.visual: wide field image of the Orion constellation
queries: Orion constellation night sky wide field

beats.text: At detonation, it will shine through broad daylight.
beats.visual: artist impression of a supernova visible in a blue daytime sky

beats.text: For months, it will glow like a half-moon.
beats.visual: artist's impression of a brilliant supernova next to the Moon in the night sky
queries: betelgeuse supernova next to moon artist impression
